data.exact_reserve_text: Reassessment of claims outstanding on underwriting years 2013 & prior (2015 - 2012 & prior) resulted in an improvement of GBP 40.5m (2015 - GBP 53.4m).

prior_year_events.event_name: Hurricane Sandy related claim (favourable court ruling)
prior_year_events.impact_description: Large release of reserves from the old 2012 account due to a favourable court ruling on a Hurricane Sandy related claim.

prior_year_events.event_name: Two Cyber facilities (better than expected experience)
prior_year_events.impact_description: Loss experience on two poorly performing Cyber facilities has not been as bad as originally expected which has allowed release of some reserves established previously.

prior_year_events.event_name: Danish court ruling on an old Energy claim
prior_year_events.impact_description: Top up of reserves on an old Energy claim when a Danish court found against underwriters in December 2016.

named_events.loss_description: Final claims from Hurricane Matthew are expected to be modest - under $8m.
The Fort McMurray wildfire loss (May 2016) also impacts 2015. Current overall reserves are C$4m; approximately 50% of this will fall back into 2015 year of account.
The main natural catastrophe to hit 2015 was the earthquake in Taiwan in February 2016.
Metrojet (Aviation) is a large risk loss impacting 2015.
Kwame Nkrumah FPSO (Upstream Energy and Marine XL - 2016) impacted the 2015 year of account.
Carrie Fisher (Accident & Health) recorded as a 2016 large risk loss.
Space X (Marine XL) recorded as a 2016 large risk loss.
LAMIA (Aviation) noted as a large risk loss in 2016.
Prince Fielder (impacts Accident & Health) noted as a large risk loss affecting 2015.
Troll Solution & Alpine Eternity (Marine & Energy Liability) noted as large risk losses impacting 2015.

data.standardized_narrative: During 2016 Syndicate 609 recorded a gross prior-year release of GBP 40.5m, principally arising from favourable development on back years. Contributing factors called out by management include a favourable court ruling on a Hurricane Sandy related claim (allowing a release from older years), better-than-expected outcomes on two Cyber facilities, partially offset by a top-up of reserves on an old Energy claim following a Danish court ruling. The release mainly affects older years (notably 2013 & prior) and impacts lines including Property, Cyber and Energy.
raw_causal_phrases: reassessment of claims outstanding on underwriting years 2013 & prior (2015 - 2012 & prior) resulted in an improvement of GBP 40.5m (2015 - GBP 53.4m).
The syndicate has continued to benefit from favorable development on the back years, contributing a saving of 11% on the loss ratio (2015 - 15%).
we were able to make a large release of reserves from the old 2012 account due to a favourable court ruling on a Hurricane Sandy related claim.
the loss experience on two poorly performing Cyber facilities has not been as bad as originally expected which has allowed us to release some of the reserves that we established last year.
Regrettably we have had to top up reserves on an old Energy claim when a Danish court found against underwriters in December 2016.

gross_premium_mix.line_of_business: Fire and other damage to property

data.data_quality_notes: Prior year movement taken from explicit sentence in claims note stating an 'improvement of GBP 40.5m' (treated as a gross release). The report includes many named losses (some quantified in foreign currencies) and an RITC for closed years; per-line prior-year quantitative breakdowns are not provided so LOB-specific amounts for the PYD are not available. The claims development triangle is present (gross, in GBP 7000s) and was not distorted by an RITC for the years used for the PYD figure, but RITC activity is present elsewhere in the report and may affect comparisons if used improperly.
